name: Risperidone
route_note: Oral tablets, ODT or solution; long-acting IM microspheres every 2 weeks; monthly or 2-monthly SC depot formulations.

discovery.note: Developed in the 1980s by combining D2 and potent 5-HT2A antagonism, building on the serotonin–dopamine antagonist concept.

tagline: Serotonin–dopamine antagonist for schizophrenia, bipolar mania and autism irritability
summary: Risperidone is a second-generation antipsychotic with potent 5-HT2A and D2 antagonism. It is used for schizophrenia, bipolar mania and irritability associated with autism, and is available in several long-acting injectable forms. Its active metabolite is marketed as paliperidone.
mechanism: Risperidone has very high 5-HT2A affinity and high D2 affinity. At lower doses the 5-HT2A blockade mitigates extrapyramidal effects, but at higher doses D2 occupancy approaches that of typical antipsychotics.
It is the antipsychotic most associated with hyperprolactinaemia, because it and 9-hydroxyrisperidone penetrate the blood–brain barrier relatively poorly and act on the pituitary outside it.
uses: Acute mania or mixed episodes in bipolar I disorder
Persistent aggression in Alzheimer's dementia (short-term, EU)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: The FDA approves Risperdal for schizophrenia in December 1993.

history.title: Risperdal Consta
history.detail: The first long-acting injectable atypical antipsychotic is approved in the US.

history.title: Bipolar mania
history.detail: Risperidone is approved for acute mania.

history.title: Autism
history.detail: Risperidone becomes the first drug approved for irritability associated with autism.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic oral risperidone launches in the US.

history.title: DOJ settlement
history.detail: Johnson & Johnson agrees to pay over $2.2 billion to resolve allegations including off-label promotion of Risperdal.

history.title: Uzedy
history.detail: Teva's subcutaneous risperidone extended-release injection is approved.

serious: Cerebrovascular events in elderly dementia patients
safety.boxed_warning: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis; not approved for this use.

facts: Risperidone was the first second-generation antipsychotic available as a long-acting injection.
